The cause is that `leaks()` searches the JSON text of the transcript, not the transcript's actual text, and JSON doubles every backslash.

In `src/leaks.py:8`, the transcript is serialized with `json.dumps(actions).lower()` before the secrets are matched. A Windows path like `C:\Users\dana` has single backslashes, but in the serialized text each one becomes `\\`. The text being searched therefore contains `c:\\users\\dana`, and the secret `c:\users\dana` never appears in it. A POSIX path has no backslashes, so `/home/dana` survives serialization unchanged and matches.

I reproduced this with the function unmodified, using `python3 -I` against `src/`:

- `cat C:\Users\dana\notes.txt` with secret `C:\Users\dana`: not flagged.
- `cat /home/dana/notes.txt` with secret `/home/dana`: flagged.

The existing tests in `tests/test_leaks.py` only cover the `/home/dana` form, so nothing catches the Windows gap. The cause is only in how the text is built and compared, so the `.lower()` call and the matching logic are not involved.

I did not change anything in `src/` or the repo. The `README.md` modification and `notes/` directory were already there before I started.
